162 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

EDWARD P. ("PINK") MONTGOMERY

The service of Prof. E. P. Montgomery as a teacher in the Savoy College was a brief interlude in his progress toward his lifework as a minister, but his record as a teacher there is highly regarded by many ex-students. The ex-students, who refer to him only as 'Pink' Montgomery, not having been known to him for a time, is not a member of the Christian church.

His ancestors, Thomas Montgomery, was a native of Ireland; his grandfather, George H. Montgomery, was born in Tennessee, in 1848, and arrived successfully in farming and stock raising and became quite wealthy at Ladonia, at the county seat of Dallas County[?]. The family moved to Alabama, where George H. Montgomery arrived in 1848. His grandfather, Thomas Montgomery, was a native of Alabama. Edward P. Montgomery, born in Tennessee, in 1848, and arrived successfully in farming. His grandfather, Thomas Montgomery, was a native of Alabama. Edward P. Montgomery was the second of five children. The family records the singular fact that 'all five of the children were educated at Savoy and that Dade is on a five year schedule.' Mr. Montgomery also published the Baptist News and became a Baptist, to which denomination he made many contributions to which denomination many years.

Martha J. Pritchett, of Virginia. Edward P. Montgomery was the second of five children.

Doctor Edward P. Montgomery, M.D.—Among the rising physicians and surgeons of the State of Texas is to be found the name of Dr. Edward P. Montgomery. He was born in Pikesville, Tennessee, and came to Texas in 1868. He was living with his father on the farm. At an early age he was sent to schools at the Savoy Male and Female College at Savoy, Texas, under Professor Halsell. In 1883 he graduated with honors at Vanderbilt University. He commenced his course of studies by reading with Dr. I. S. King in the subject a portion of 1887, the subject was part of 1887, the young doctor started out a successful career as a practitioner and as a teacher.
